questions.explain: The taxonomy defines metrics as numeric time-series (CPU, queries per second, cache hit ratio), logs as structured/semi-structured event records, traces as causal chains through parse/plan/execute/fetch, and events as discrete semantically meaningful occurrences like schema changes or failovers.
options: Metrics, logs, traces, and events
Snapshots, backups, restores, and replays

questions.explain: sys.dm_os_wait_stats is cumulative since service restart, so models should train on deltas between scrapes rather than absolute values; the PromQL rate() function handles that conversion.
options: It can only be queried once per day
It requires a table lock to read
Values must be doubled before use
It is cumulative since the last service restart, so models should train on deltas between scrapes
questions.q: Why does the chapter state that anomaly models must train on deltas (not absolute values) of sys.dm_os_wait_stats?

questions.explain: Encoding hour as raw integers 0-23 breaks continuity between hour 23 and hour 0; sine/cosine encoding on a circle preserves temporal adjacency, making the model seasonality-aware without full decomposition.
options: It makes the model train faster
It reduces the number of features needed
It preserves the temporal adjacency between hour 23 and hour 0 so the model is seasonality-aware
It is required by Isolation Forest for numerical input
questions.q: Why does the chapter's Isolation Forest example encode hour_of_day and day_of_week as sine/cosine pairs rather than raw integers?

questions.explain: The chapter separates automation into tiers: tier one actions (UPDATE STATISTICS, index creation during non-production hours, connection pool adjustments) can be automated with post-execution logging, while tier two actions require explicit DBA approval before execution.
options: Tier one actions like UPDATE STATISTICS and connection pool adjustments can be automated with post-execution logging
All actions recommended by the AI should execute immediately
Tier one actions must always wait for human approval
No database action may ever be automated
questions.q: Under the chapter's two-tier automation model, which statement is correct?

questions.explain: The chapter advises training on at least one full business cycle before enabling production alerting, plus a feedback mechanism where the DBA marks alerts as expected behavior and the model retrains on that event class.
options: Delete the model and retrain from scratch daily
Lower the contamination parameter to zero
Switch to random threshold guessing
Train on at least one full business cycle before enabling production alerting and add a DBA feedback mechanism to retrain on expected-behavior events
questions.q: What mitigation does the chapter give for alert fatigue caused by an anomaly model firing on recurring events like month-end batch jobs it has never seen?
